GruntWorx should inherit Instead’s operational safeguards, while defining its own vendor limits and mappings.

1. **Rate limits: budget at both connection and app level.** Instead throttles per connection/API group, then across the app. The order matters: a request rejected by its group must not consume an app slot. Defaults are **5 docs requests/minute**, **50 entity requests/minute**, and **500 app requests/minute**; these are Instead settings, not GruntWorx requirements. Honor `Retry-After` as seconds or an HTTP date. Ordinary operations allow **10 retries**, but throttling reschedules work with a reset counter—this is **not a wall-clock deadline**. Give GruntWorx its own throttle keys and worker subclass. [Throttle implementation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/initializers/sidekiq.rb:102), [retry policy](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/operation_worker.rb:10).

2. **Lost webhooks: reconcile against vendor truth.** Instead’s sweep is designed for every **30 minutes**, selecting uploaded documents still `sent` after **1 hour** or `processing` after **12 hours**, within a **2-day window**. Older records remain unchanged; disconnected or unavailable providers are skipped. Reconciliation reads paginated folders, then individually looks up documents absent from those pages; an individual 404 becomes `archived`. Reconciliation jobs have **zero retries** because the next sweep retries eligible records. Both webhook and polling updates use the same status application service, which ignores duplicates and refuses backward transitions. GruntWorx needs equivalent read-back capabilities and explicit recovery-window choices. [Eligibility bounds](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/queries/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_candidates_query.rb:8), [pagination/fallback](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_statuses_worker.rb:43), [shared status handling](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/apply_processing_status.rb:35).

3. **Failure reasons: preserve the common vocabulary.** Existing reasons are `unexpected`, `no_active_connection`, `network_error`, `unauthorized`, `api_error`, `exceeded`, `forbidden`, and `encrypted`. Separate transient errors from terminal refusals: quota exhaustion maps to `exceeded`, authentication failures to `unauthorized`, and other terminal API refusals generally to `api_error`. Instead maps `password_required` to `encrypted`; unknown processing failures retain an error status without inventing a reason. Successful recovery clears old reasons. GruntWorx should translate its errors into these meanings and report contract/configuration failures for engineering attention. [Vocabulary and transitions](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:15), [refusal mapping](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/refusals_helper.rb:24).

4. **Signed-URL cassettes: treat recorded upload credentials as secrets.** The VCR hook scrubs policies, AWS credentials/signatures, and client secrets from request and response bodies; Instead OAuth tokens and bearer headers receive vendor-host-specific filtering. Extend that filtering for GruntWorx’s host and credential formats. Replay freezes time at the cassette’s recording timestamp so signed-target expiry stays deterministic; new recordings use real time. Client specs use live recordings for reproducible exchanges and HTTP stubs for responses the developer account cannot produce. [Scrubbing](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/spec_helper.rb:164), [cassette clock](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/support/vcr_fixed_time.rb:3), [client-spec approach](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/unit/tax_preparation/lib/tax_automations/instead/client_spec.rb:5).

5. **Entity matching: reuse identity conservatively.** Instead first supports local lookup by firm, account/contact, and entity type, reusing an entity across tax years. Name linking considers only active, unlinked entities in the same firm/type and links **exactly one** match. It normalizes punctuation, whitespace, case and business legal-form spellings; person matching permits swapped names only after no ordinary match, and account-name fallback only for a sole contact. Ambiguous matches stay unlinked and produce metrics. Preserve these boundaries: creating an Instead entity is explicitly non-idempotent, so local deduplication does not guarantee safe retries after an uncertain vendor response. Establish GruntWorx’s identity and idempotency guarantees explicitly. [Local identity lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/find_entity.rb:28), [matching rules](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/link_entity_by_name.rb:49), [creation semantics](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/create_entity.rb:3).

These are findings from the existing code; GruntWorx’s actual API capabilities and limits still need validation. No files were edited.
